title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 70
paragraphs: So when the word was passed to put to sea, they brought their ships out toward Salamis and quietly arranged themselves along the shore in their various positions. Daylight was no longer sufficient at that hour for them to engage, night having come on; but they made their preparations to fight the next day. Meanwhile the Greeks were seized with fear and dismay, especially those from the Peloponnese. They were dismayed because, remaining at Salamis, they were to fight a battle on behalf of the Athenians' land, and if defeated they would be cut off from escape and blockaded on an island, while leaving their own country undefended. And indeed the barbarians' land-army was marching forward that very night toward the Peloponnese.
